narrative:
The model determined that you have a 27% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were your savings situation, your other installment plans, and the purpose of the loan. Your lack of any known savings was the most important reason pushing the model toward viewing you as higher risk. Having no savings stands out compared with many approved applicants who typically have at least some modest reserves. This absence of a financial buffer raised significant concern about your ability to handle unexpected difficulties while repaying the loan.

Next, the fact that you already have other installment plans with a bank worked against you, pulling the prediction further toward bad credit risk. This suggested you already carry debt obligations that could stretch your finances too thin.

Your request for a used-car loan, however, actually helped your case somewhat by pushing the prediction back toward the good-credit side. Used-car financing is generally seen as lower risk than some other purposes.

Given these factors, particularly your limited savings and existing debt payments, you should focus on building up savings, reducing your current installment commitments if possible, and perhaps waiting until your overall financial picture looks more stable before reapplying. This would likely improve your chances in a future application. (218 words)
